question: In the initial years of independence, the state had complete control of those industries that were:

options.text: only complementary to the policies of the private sector

solution:
The correct answer is __**vital for the economy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the initial years of independence, the Indian government took control of key industries to ensure the security and stability of the economy.
 
• These industries included sectors such as defense, railways, atomic energy, and heavy industries.
 
• The government aimed to foster economic growth and self-reliance by managing industries that were crucial for national development.
 
• State control helped in regulating these industries, ensuring equitable distribution of resources, and preventing monopoly practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nationalization**

 
 
• Nationalization refers to the process by which the government takes control of private industry or assets and converts them into public ownership.
 
• This was a common practice in many newly independent countries to ensure control over critical sectors.
 
• India nationalized several key industries and banks to build a robust economic structure.
 
 
 
• **Mixed Economy**
 
 
• India adopted a mixed economy model post-independence, combining elements of both capitalism and socialism.
 
• This model allowed both private and public sectors to coexist, with the state playing a significant role in guiding economic development.
 
• It aimed at achieving balanced economic growth, reducing inequalities, and providing public welfare.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• India's economic planning through Five-Year Plans focused on strategic sectors to achieve rapid industrialization and economic growth.
 
• The plans included development targets and resource allocation strategies for various sectors, emphasizing state control over vital industries.
 
• These plans were instrumental in shaping India's economic policies and industrial base in the initial years of independence.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**
 
 
• PSUs are government-owned corporations or state-owned enterprises created to undertake commercial activities on behalf of the government.
 
• They play a crucial role in the economic development of the country, especially in sectors critical to national interest.
 
• PSUs like Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) were established to strengthen India's industrial base.
